forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Epsom and Ewell's three-year funding gap falls from £5.063m to £0.579m, 2026/27 budget balanced
news_drafts.lead:
Epsom and Ewell Borough Council's three-year funding gap has fallen from £5.063m to £0.579m, and its budget for 2026/27 is balanced. The figures are in the external auditors' annual report on value for money for the year ended 31 March 2026, which went to the Audit and Scrutiny Committee on 12 November.

The report attributes the reduction to updated funding assumptions, expenditure reductions and planned efficiencies. It gives no split between the three.

The remaining £0.579m is made up of £0.206m in 2027/28 and £0.373m in 2028/29. According to the report, both residual gaps will transfer to East Surrey Council after vesting day.

news_drafts.headline: Epsom and Ewell reports £250k Q1 overspend on nightly paid housing despite budget for 100 households
news_drafts.lead:
Epsom and Ewell Borough Council is forecasting a £250,000 overspend on housing in the first quarter of 2026/27, after demand for nightly paid accommodation for homeless households rose beyond what it had budgeted for. The council's quarter one budget monitoring report (the in-year check of spending against budget) says the overspend will be covered by corporate contingency, money held centrally for unforeseen costs.

The council had raised its 2026/27 budget to provide for an average of 100 households in nightly paid accommodation. The report says demand "dramatically increased" in the first quarter as landlords responded to the Renters Rights Act, which came into force in May. The overspend sits within a total budget of £11.868m.

The paper says a £750,000 growth budget was put into the nightly paid service for 2026/27 "to address some of the structural deficit in this area". The budget has since been increased by a further £128,500 in the year, funded from the council's inflationary provision. The council's chief finance officer (the section 151 officer, who has a legal duty to warn if the council cannot balance its books) describes the position as "highly sensitive to fluctuations in demand, availability of accommodation and wider housing market conditions."

news_drafts.headline: Epsom and Ewell halts capital investment following government reorganization announcement
news_drafts.lead: Epsom and Ewell council has ceased acquisitions under its Commercial Property Investment Fund following the government's 28 October announcement that Surrey's current county, district and borough councils will be replaced by two unitary authorities. The council had estimated £49.6m capital expenditure on commercial properties for 2025/26 but made no property purchases, spending £2.8m against a total capital forecast of £58.3m. Meanwhile, the council's treasury performance improved: net investment income reached £1,178,313, exceeding its mid-year forecast by £236,313 despite lower average cash balances and declining interest rates. The council's average net return on investments was 4.23%, outperforming the SONIA benchmark. The council maintained its Public Works Loan Board debt flat at £64.4m and required no temporary borrowing during the year.

findings.paper_title: EEBC Internal Audit Progress Report 2026-27 - Oct 26 FINAL
findings.headline: HR recruitment and capacity review removed from the plan as recruitment moves to the new East Surrey Unitary Council.
findings.detail: The planned HR Recruitment and Capacity review was withdrawn. The report says recruitment 'will naturally start fall within the remit of the new East Surrey Unitary Council' as the council moves towards vesting day.
findings.matters: A finance director at a council facing reorganisation would see a concrete example of staffing and recruitment responsibility moving to a successor authority, with audit coverage following the change.
findings.quote: recruitment will naturally start fall within the remit of the new East Surrey Unitary Council.

findings.paper_title: EEBC Internal Audit Progress Report 2026-27 - Oct 26 FINAL
findings.headline: IT follow-up cancelled to free up staff for firewall review, citing demands of IT staff leading into vesting day.
findings.detail: The IT follow-up review was cancelled to let internal resources focus on the Firewall Management and Monitoring review. The report cites the demands on IT staff leading into vesting day, and that there are no prior-year limited assurance reviews needing detailed follow-up.
findings.matters: Councils reorganising into unitary authorities are reallocating scarce staff and audit time, and other finance directors facing similar transitions would want to see how audit coverage was prioritised.
findings.quote: In recognition of the demands of IT staff leading into vesting day

findings.paper_title: EEBC Internal Audit Progress Report 2026-27 - Oct 26 FINAL
findings.headline: No overdue high-priority management actions; 2 low-priority and 4 medium-priority actions are overdue.
findings.detail: Annex 1 states there are no overdue high-priority actions. Annex 2 lists the overdue low and medium-priority actions, mainly from the Use of Volunteers (Limited, Nov 2025), Payroll (Reasonable, Nov 2025) and Vacancy Management (Reasonable, May 2026) reviews, with several revised due dates marked as TBC or 'No update'.
findings.matters: Overdue actions on Payroll and Vacancy Management touch the council's largest cost base, and a finance director would want to see whether the revised dates are met.
findings.quote: There are no overdue ‘high priority’ management actions.

findings.paper_title: EEBC Internal Audit Progress Report 2026-27 - Oct 26 FINAL
findings.headline: No audit reports with 'Limited' or 'No' assurance published since the previous progress report.
findings.detail: The report states that no reports with a limited or no assurance opinion were published since the previous progress report. Earlier 'Limited' opinions, including Use of Volunteers, remain on the live audit list.
findings.matters: A finance director would note that the council has no new 'Limited' or 'No' opinions in this period, though older limited-assurance areas remain open.
findings.quote: There have been no reports published with a ‘limited’ or ‘no’ assurance opinion since our previous progress report.

findings.paper_title: EEBC Internal Audit Progress Report 2026-27 - Oct 26 FINAL
findings.headline: Accounts Receivable and Debt Management audit given a 'Reasonable' assurance opinion, with 3 medium-priority actions agreed.
findings.detail: The Accounts Receivable and Debt Management review was finalised in August 2026 with a Reasonable opinion, which the paper describes as 'Some issues, non-compliance or scope for improvement were identified'. The management actions table shows 3 medium-priority actions agreed, all pending.
findings.matters: Debt recovery directly affects the council's income and bad debt provision, so a finance director would want to see whether the recorded improvement actions are delivered.
findings.quote: Accounts Receivable and Debt management Aug 2026 DofCS Reasonable
